newsitem.title: UK: Spain sets cap on Eurobond, possibly by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Spain sets cap on Eurobond, possibly by year-end.

text.p: Spain is rumoured to be eyeing the mark sector for a jumbo Eurobond issue but syndicate managers said the country should leave the launch until next year.
"They definitely have their eye on a European currency," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank in London said.
But the recent poor performance of some mark-denominated offerings meant it was not the best time to issue a bond.
"One thing for sure is that at these levels and at this time of year you have to be much more generous," a trader said.
But Spain -- said to want a payment date before the end of the year possibly due to its low profile in the international capital market this year -- was anxious to launch a bond, they added.
New issues traders said several banks were bidding for the yet-to-be awarded Spanish mandate.
"Banks are showing Spain several currencies -- dollars, Ecu, marks and sterling," a syndicate manager said.
"Marks seem particularly likely. But we are still in the very early stages. Spain is looking for size, 1.5 to 2.0 billion marks in the five to 10-year sector," another trader said.
At a five-year mark maturity, he said Spain was likely to pay three-month LIBOR flat all-in and at 10 years marginally over LIBOR.
"It will depend on what the banks are prepared to show them and how greedy they (Spain) are," he said.
Dealers said recent 500 million mark five-year deals for Denmark, the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank (IADB) had not performed well and spreads had widened.
"Denmark was a disaster. It widened by 10 basis points and the World Bank and IADB widened by around six b.p.," said a syndicate manager at a German bank.
The Denmark deal was launched 22 b.p. over government paper, the IADB at 20 b.p. over and the World Bank at a 16 b.p. spread.
The European Investment Bank was also said to be eyeing the mark sector but syndicate managers said the same about it.
"The EIB is responsible enough not to go for a launch before next year. They want to have a more strategic approach," a syndicate manager said.
"For the Eurobond market the end of the year is just about here already. Activity in the market will soon slow down significantly," she added.
"There's really just next week left where you can reasonably launch a deal. There may be one or two opportunisitc deals before the year end but otherwise we wait for next year."
Spain launched two international bonds this year, a 9.0 billion French franc 10-year bond issued in two tranches and a 150 billion yen 10-year.
